newsitem.title: CANADA: Global output, subsidies to hit grains - Ag Canada.
newsitem.headline: Global output, subsidies to hit grains - Ag Canada.

text.p: Record Prairie grain output along with higher world production and renewed European Union export subsidies should all weigh on world grain values, Agriculture Canada said in its October economic analysis.

"World wheat and barley prices have been pressured by prospects for higher global production. Export subsidies are expected to be a factor in 1996/97 (Aug/July) since the EU has begun subsidizing wheat and barley exports," Ag Canada said.
Canadian milling wheat prices in crop year 1996/97 were forecast by Ag Canada to range from C$217 to C$237 a tonne, down from the average price of C$254 a tonne in 1995/96.
Canadian barley prices were seen ranging from C$135-155, down from C$170 last year.
Total Prairie grain and oilseed production was forecast by Ag Canada at a record 53.6 million tonnes, up 16 percent from the previous year's output of 46.2 million tonnes.
The number was above the Canadian Wheat Board's Sept 12 forecast for Prairie output at 52.8 million tonnes. The previous record for Prairie output was in 1986 at 51 million tonnes.
Speculation the United States may resume it Export Enhancement Program subsidy before the current crop year ends may also weigh on prices, Ag Canada said.

"Other factors to watch which will have a major influence on grain and oilseed prices in 1996/97 are the size and quality of the 1996 U.S. corn and soybean crops, China's import demand, and the 1997 U.S. winter wheat crop," the Ag Canada release said.
